newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech PM calls Oct 8 meeting to discuss trade gap.
newsitem.headline: Czech PM calls Oct 8 meeting to discuss trade gap.

text.p: Czech Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus said on Wednesday the January-August trade deficit of over 100 billion crowns was high, and said he would call a special ministerial meeting on October 8 to discuss ways to reduce the widening trade gap.
"This figure is high, and I asked five members of the cabinet to prepare analytical materials on this ... and proposals on what to do..." Klaus told a news conference after a regular cabinet meeting.
He said he expected the ministers to discuss the topic on October 8.

The Czech Statistical Bureau earlier on Wednesday said the August trade deficit of 14.7 billion crowns took the January-August trade gap to a record 100.9 billion crowns from 59.5 billion crowns in the same period last year.
The government has repeatedly ruled out a devaluation of the Czech crown to boost exports. Klaus did not say what measures might be proposed at the meeting.

A government spokesman said later that Industry and Trade Minister Vladimir Dlouhy, Finance Minister Ivan Kocarnik, Agriculture Minister Josef Lux, Czech National Bank Governor Josef Tosovsky, and Czech Statistical Bureau Chairman Edvard Outrata would join Klaus for the meeting.
